study.title: Exploring the potential central regulatory mechanisms of acupuncture for acute-stage Bell's palsy: an fMRI-based investigation
study.study_design: experimental intervention; pre-post single-arm acupuncture group with healthy control comparison; resting-state fMRI collected before and after treatment in BP patients; single scan in healthy controls
study.blinding: outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation and treatment status; fMRI data analysts were blinded to group allocation and time points during preprocessing and statistical analysis; blinding of acupuncturists was not feasible
study.population: Individuals with acute Bell's facial paralysis (within 1–7 days of onset) and healthy controls matched by age, sex, and handedness
study.disease_condition: acute Bell's palsy (BP); acute idiopathic peripheral facial paralysis
study.inclusion_criteria: Acute BP patients: Diagnosed with Bell's facial paralysis based on established diagnostic criteria (Jia, 2013); first-time unilateral BP with an H-B facial nerve grade higher than I but lower than VI, with symptom onset within the past 7 days; no acupuncture treatment received in the past 3 months; aged between 16 and 65 years, of any sex, right-handed; years of education ≥12 years; routine MRI scans show no significant intracranial abnormalities; eligible for MRI scanning (i.e., no metal dental work, pacemakers, stents, or claustrophobia); normal mental and behavioral status, without major systemic diseases; and provided voluntary informed consent and were able to comply with and complete the acupuncture treatment. Healthy subjects: Healthy individuals matched in age, sex, years of education, and other characteristics with the BP patients, right-handed; no acupuncture treatment within the past 3 months; normal neurological examination findings, no evident abnormalities on routine MRI scans, and no personal or family history of neurological or psychiatric disorders; eligible for MRI scanning (i.e., no metal dental work, pacemakers, stents, or claustrophobia); and voluntarily signed informed consent.
study.exclusion_criteria: Acute BP patients: Individuals with facial paralysis secondary to other conditions (e.g., tumors, trauma, or otitis media); those with comorbid underlying diseases, severe organic disorders of major organs, or mental disorders; pregnant or breastfeeding women; and those with poor compliance or inability to complete the study. Healthy subjects: Individuals with underlying diseases, severe organic disorders of major organs, or mental disorders; pregnant or lactating women; those with a history of facial trauma, otitis media, or viral infection (e.g., herpes simplex) within the past 3 months; those with a family history of neurological diseases (not limited to BP); and individuals currently taking medications that affect central nervous system function (e.g., antidepressants, corticosteroids).

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: acupoints on the affected side (face) and bilateral LI4 (Hegu) on the hands
interventions.laterality_exact: affected side for facial acupoints; bilateral for LI4 (Hegu)
interventions.needle_type_exact: Disposable acupuncture needles (Wujiang Yunlong Medical Equipment Co., Ltd., Su Jizhun 20142200226)
interventions.penetration_exact: skin penetration; needles inserted to specified depths
interventions.depth_exact: ST2: 10–15 mm perpendicularly; GB14: 20–25 mm toward EX-HN4 region; ST8: 10–15 mm horizontally in upward direction; SI18: 10–15 mm obliquely toward anterior aspect of lower root of ear on affected side; SJ17: 12–20 mm perpendicularly; SI18 (second mention): 12–20 mm perpendicularly; ST6 and ST4: 15–20 mm bidirectionally; LI4: 12–20 mm perpendicularly
interventions.manipulation_exact: needle manipulated until Deqi achieved; needles retained for 30 min
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Yes; Deqi defined as simultaneous occurrence of: (1) needle sensations reported by the patient (e.g., soreness, numbness, distension, heaviness) and (2) a tight, rough sensation under the needle perceived by the acupuncturist (i.e., 'needle sensation')
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: three times per week (Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday) until day 28 of the disease course
interventions.treatment_period_exact: until the 28th day from the onset of symptoms; if cured within 28-day period, treatment concluded early; if not, treatment continued beyond that point
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: all acupuncture procedures were carried out by the same practitioner, who had more than 3 years of clinical experience
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: In accordance with the guidelines outlined in Acupuncture (Liang and Wang, 2016)

sensory_interoceptive_responses.instrument_name_exact: not_reported; Deqi defined by study criteria
sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: soreness, numbness, distension, heaviness (patient-reported); tight, rough sensation under needle (acupuncturist-perceived)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: Deqi was achieved (required for needle retention to proceed); specific quantitative values not reported
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was a procedural requirement, not a quantitatively measured outcome. No formal Deqi scale was administered.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Structural: 3D T1 BRAVO sequence; Functional: gradient echo planar imaging sequence
neuroimaging_methods.TR_exact: Structural: TR = 8.2 ms; Functional: TR = 2000 ms
neuroimaging_methods.TE_exact: Structural: TE = 3.2 ms; Functional: TE = 30 ms
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: Structural: slice thickness = 1.0 mm, slice gap = 1.0 mm; Functional: voxel size = 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Structural: 5 min and 36 s; Functional: 6 min and 10 s
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: DPABI software package within MATLAB R2017b; initial conversion: dcm2niigui
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum of 6 mm × 6 mm × 6 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Head motion quantified using framewise displacement (FD). Time points with FD > 0.5 mm were excluded, and participants with >20% of time points discarded were removed from further analysis. Both mean FD and maximum rotation angle were calculated, and datasets with head motion exceeding 3 mm or 3° were excluded.
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: Temporal filtering to retain low-frequency signals with the range 0.01–0.08 Hz
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-level P < 0.001 and cluster-level P < 0.01 (GRF correction)
Figure captions state: corrected for GRF with voxel P < 0.001, cluster P < 0.05
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Gaussian random field (GRF) theory with thresholds set at voxel-level P < 0.001 and cluster-level P < 0.01

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture control group was included. The authors acknowledge this as a study limitation: 'this study did not include a sham acupuncture group as a control; therefore, the interference of the natural course of recovery and the placebo effect cannot be completely ruled out.'
Expectancy, credibility, and formal blinding success measures were not assessed or reported for participants.

Table 8 (fALFF differences after vs before treatment in BP patients) lists only two brain regions: Left medial superior frontal gyrus and Left precentral gyrus. However, the abstract and Figure 6 caption also mention 'Right angular gyrus' (increased fALFF). No coordinate row for the Right angular gyrus appears in Table 8. The text in Results section states 'the fALFF value of the left precentral gyrus and the right angular gyrus increased' but Table 8 does not include this coordinate row. This discrepancy is flagged.

The statistical threshold reported in the Methods (section 2.8) states 'voxel-level P < 0.001 and cluster-level P < 0.01,' but Figure captions throughout the paper state 'corrected for GRF with voxel P < 0.001, cluster P < 0.05.' This inconsistency is present across the paper and both thresholds are preserved in extraction.

The right posterior cingulate gyrus coordinate MNI Y = -43 appears in Table 4. The brain region label includes 'Right' in the table but the MNI X coordinate is 3, which is near midline. This is preserved as reported.
No correlation analyses between clinical scale scores and neuroimaging metrics (fALFF, ReHo) were conducted or reported. The authors note this as a limitation.
No long-term follow-up neuroimaging data were collected. The observation period ended at day 28.

The paper uses both 'anterior central gyrus' and 'precentral gyrus' to refer to the same structure in the Discussion. These are treated as equivalent and region names are preserved exactly as they appear in tables versus text.

Table 9 reports identical t-values (-3.480) for both Right medial superior frontal gyrus and Left medial superior frontal gyrus. This appears as printed in the original paper and is preserved as reported.

The number of fMRI sessions per patient is not explicitly stated as a numeric count. The treatment schedule was three sessions per week for up to 28 days (i.e., approximately 12 sessions), but patients cured earlier stopped early, so actual session counts varied. This is not computed or inferred in the interventions field.
No deqi quantification instrument (e.g., MASS, MGQ, SSSQ) was used. Deqi was defined operationally as a procedural criterion rather than a measured outcome.

The abstract states 'decreased ReHo in the right middle frontal gyrus' for the post-treatment vs HC comparison, and Table 7 and Figure 5 confirm this. However, the Discussion also references this region. All are consistent and extracted.

The paper reports the healthy control group underwent only a single fMRI scan with no clinical outcome assessments. HC neuroimaging data serve only as between-group comparisons, not longitudinal controls.
